parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The unit is a single file, src/auth/entity/user.entity.ts, and it covers one concern: the UserEntity. That includes its persisted fields (identity, profile, status, token and 2FA state, role relation) and how its password is handled. All of these are part of the user aggregate, so the file does not split into unrelated concerns. Password logic is kept on the entity: hashPassword() is the single place that changes the password. Both lifecycle hooks, hashPasswordBeforeInsert and hashPasswordBeforeUpdate, call hashPassword() rather than calling bcrypt themselves.

Two minor points:
- Both hooks repeat the same guard, `this.password && !this.skipHashPassword`.
- validatePassword calls bcrypt.hash(password, this.salt) directly. This differs from hashPassword(), which changes the entity's state, so it is not really a bypass.

Both points are small, sit next to each other in one file, and do not scatter the rule across modules. Overall the file is cohesive and uses its own abstractions consistently.
